_comment: Measured on THIS board at MCK 78 MHz. A record of one board, not a
datasheet: re-measure rather than re-derive if any of it is in doubt.
Tolerances come from the observed run-to-run spread. A tolerance
tighter than the spread is a flaky test; one much looser is not a test.
The DAC span and ADVREF used to live here and now live in
calibration.json at the repository root, read through
host/calibration.py. They are measurements of the hardware,
not expectations about its behaviour, and four things
outside tests/ were reaching in here to get them.
lib/due_shared/src/fw_version.h, which both tracks compile.
It used to be two hand-copied files and the string drifted from
the numbers; the string is derived now. Bump both together: a
board reporting a version this file does not know about is
either a stale flash or an un-updated baseline, and the test
cannot tell you which if only one of them moved.
Floors, not bands. Measured five 4 s runs per mode on this board:
in-dma 19.8-30.5, out-dma 17.9-28.2, duplex-dma 8.2-20.0 MB/s, a
run-to-run spread of 35-59%. That is far wider than the ~5% this
project's notes previously recorded, so a floor near the typical
figure is a flaky test, not a strict one. What these have to catch
is a collapse - the ~1.7 MB/s gated-OUT regime that once blocked
full-rate duplex - and they still catch it by a factor of three or
more.

transport_measured_mbs._comment: Observed range, five 4 s runs per mode, 2026-08-22.

_comment: Underruns tolerated per ladder run.
Zero is the requirement and nothing else is acceptable in the end.
But host-fed playback sporadically underruns at rates that are
otherwise clean - 2 and 3 in a both-track run at RC 86 and RC 50,
which pass 5/5 on their own - while the rates that genuinely
starve give 15 to 50. A tolerance of 5 separates that tail from a
real collapse, so the ladders stay usable as a regression gate
instead of failing at random.
This used to say to remove it when objective 0 closed. Objective 0
was the lost-sample defect and it has closed, but this is not its
tail: an underrun is the ring running dry, not data going missing.
It belongs to the feed policy in objective 0a, which is open.
Whether it is still needed has not been retested since the fix -
measure before removing it.
Main-loop load, measured on THIS board with the cycle-counter
monitor (bsp/load.c). Idle and steady-state capture both put
essentially every pass in one log2 bucket, which is what makes
an outlier meaningful. Floors are well below the measured rate
because the point is to catch a loop that has stopped running,
not to police a few per cent of drift.
The idle pass went 9.72 -> 7.90 -> 6.70 us as ctl_service and then
usb_cdc_poll were gated to 1 kHz. Both were reading a UOTGHS
register every pass to ask about events that happen tens of times
a second. load_tick itself is free at this resolution: 128.1 k with
it against 127.4 k built out. Re-measure rather than scale.
These are Track B's. The monitor is shared from 2026-08-28 and
the suite runs on both tracks; the floors are loose enough to
cover both, but the loops are NOT the same. Track A idles at
75.1 k passes/s against Track B's 160.4 k on this bench - a 2.14x
difference that is its own finding, open in issue #13. Do not
read a Track A number against idle_passes_per_s below.
